planting.note: Plant divisions in fall into humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, giving the spreading rhizomes room to run.

directions: Epimedium elongatum is a woodland species from western Sichuan, China, that travels by a moderately long creeping rhizome and in time forms a loose spreading colony rather than a tight clump. In late spring, tall arching panicles carry an unusually large number of flowers, sometimes two to three dozen per stem, each bright yellow and about an inch across with a slender spur that curves upward or spreads horizontally. Site it in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in dappled to full shade, where its height and spreading habit give it a looser, more naturalistic presence than the tidy clump-forming epimediums. Once established it tolerates competition from tree roots and short dry spells, but flowers and colors best with consistent moisture through spring.
sources: Plants of the World Online (Kew Science)

common_name: Yellow Princess Epimedium (Late-Blooming Light Yellow Barrenwort)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall into humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; this selection breaks dormancy later than most grandiflorum forms.

directions: 'Yellow Princess' is a named Epimedium grandiflorum selection from the Garden Vision Epimediums breeding program, chosen for emerging and flowering later than most grandiflorum cultivars, which stretches the barrenwort bloom season into late spring. Small, neat leaflets stay low at around five and a half inches, while wiry stems lift clean, clear light-yellow flowers up to ten inches, holding them well above the foliage mat. Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, and keep soil evenly moist during the spring growth flush since foliage emerges later and has less time to toughen before summer heat arrives. Its compact size and soft color make it a good front-of-border companion to earlier-blooming epimediums, extending interest without repeating their look.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall into humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; site where the downward-facing flowers can be viewed from below or on a slope.

directions: 'Chocolate Lace' is a Garden Vision Epimediums selection of Epimedium grandiflorum f. flavescens grown chiefly for its spring foliage, which emerges in rich milk-chocolate tones before settling into green overlaid with fine burgundy tracery and deep purple margins. Large creamy, yellow-green flowers open in mid spring but are carried low, often tucked beneath the foliage canopy rather than held above it, so part the leaves or view the clump from a raised bed to appreciate them fully. It does not produce a second flush of bloom, so its lasting appeal through the season comes from the patterned leaf color rather than repeat flowering. Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade with consistent moisture in spring, and comb out old foliage before new growth emerges to keep the leaf pattern looking fresh.

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall into humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; foliage stays semi-evergreen in milder climates.

directions: 'Passion Hearts' is a Garden Vision Epimediums selection of the clump-forming Japanese species Epimedium sempervirens, named for its elongated, heart-shaped leaflets and dramatic spring color change. New foliage opens deep chocolate-brown, warms through vibrant red tones over several weeks, and finally settles into green with a persistent darker edge, giving the mound months of changing interest beyond bloom. In mid spring, generous clusters of medium-sized flowers with light lavender sepals and slender spurs rise above the tidy, non-running clump. Grow in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial to full shade, and expect foliage to remain semi-evergreen in milder winters, tidied up in early spring before new growth and flowers appear.
